action_criteria.expected_evidence: Evans index 0.41, DESH, callosal angle 68 degrees, temporal horns enlarged, prominent aqueductal flow void, no obstruction; Fazekas 2, MTA 1
action_criteria.label: Brain MRI with the iNPH markers
action_criteria.rationale: MRI must show ventriculomegaly out of proportion to atrophy, the supportive features and no obstruction before any CSF is removed.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Normal blood count, electrolytes, creatinine, TSH and vitamin B12; RPR and HIV non-reactive
action_criteria.label: Targeted labs for reversible contributors
action_criteria.rationale: Blood tests do not diagnose iNPH; they only screen for thyroid, B12, syphilis or metabolic contributors to the cognitive decline.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: TUG 31 s, 10-metre walk 26 s, 180-degree turn in 13 steps, magnetic shuffling gait with freezing, en-bloc turn, 3-step retropulsion without falling
action_criteria.label: Baseline timed gait assessment before the tap
action_criteria.rationale: The tap and drainage responses can only be judged against objective TUG and 10-metre walk times recorded before CSF is removed.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: MoCA 21/30 with visuospatial-executive, attention and abstraction errors, free recall 1/5 improving to 4/5 with cues
action_criteria.label: Bedside cognitive screen
action_criteria.rationale: A baseline MoCA documents the executive and retrieval deficits and gives the post-tap and post-drainage scores a reference.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Opening pressure 14 cmH2O, normal cells, protein and glucose; 45 mL removed; TUG 31 s at baseline, 30 s at 2 hours, 31 s at 4 and 24 hours; 10-metre walk and MoCA unchanged
action_criteria.label: Lumbar tap test with opening pressure
action_criteria.rationale: The opening pressure and CSF content confirm normal-pressure, bland CSF, and the timed gait after 45 mL removal tests CSF responsiveness.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: TUG 30 s at 2 hours, 31 s at 4 and 24 hours (0%), 10-metre walk 26 s, MoCA 21/30, urgency unchanged
action_criteria.label: Post-tap timed gait reassessment
action_criteria.rationale: Repeating the same timed measures after CSF removal is what shows that this single tap produced no gait change.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: About 420 mL drained over 72 hours; TUG 31 s to 28 s on day 1, 23 s on day 2 and 19 s on day 3 (39%); 10-metre walk 26 to 16 s; MoCA 21 to 24; no incontinence
action_criteria.label: Extended lumbar drainage after the negative tap
action_criteria.rationale: With a full syndrome and DESH but no response to a single tap, a 72-hour drainage trial is the more sensitive test of CSF responsiveness.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not diagnose iNPH from ventriculomegaly alone: the diagnosis needs the clinical syndrome (gait disturbance with cognitive or urinary symptoms) and supportive imaging, with no other cause explaining them [Relkin_2005]
Do not exclude shunt-responsive iNPH on a single negative tap test: its sensitivity is 26% to 61% [Marmarou_2005]
Do not attribute the gait disorder to knee osteoarthritis: a magnetic, freezing gait with en-bloc turns and normal strength is not an arthritic gait
required_recommendations: Do not stop at the single negative tap test; proceed to extended lumbar drainage (about 10 mL/hour, 300 to 500 mL over 72 hours) with daily timed gait measures, which has a higher sensitivity than the tap test (50% to 100% versus 26% to 61%) [Marmarou_2005]

Refer to neurosurgery for CSF shunting with a programmable valve, on the basis of the extended lumbar drainage response (TUG 31 to 19 s, 39%, on day 3), the DESH-pattern MRI and normal-pressure CSF [Nakajima_2021]
Falls-prevention measures (physiotherapy, home assessment, walking aid) while awaiting surgery

avoided_actions.rationale: EEG has no role in a chronic gait and cognitive syndrome without seizures or fluctuating awareness
There is no syncope, palpitation or cardiac question in this gait and cognitive work-up
Echocardiography answers no question in this work-up: there is no cardioembolic event or heart failure
Head CT adds nothing once brain MRI is available, which measures the ventricles, callosal angle and DESH better
Rhythm monitoring has no role: his falls are gait falls, without syncope or palpitations
Molecular or advanced imaging does not change the iNPH decision, which rests on MRI and the tap and drainage tests
A full neuropsychological battery is not needed for the iNPH decision; the bedside screen and timed gait measures are
Prion, inflammatory and infectious CSF assays answer no question in an 18-month afebrile gait syndrome with bland CSF

differential.key_features: The single tap produced no change, but TUG improved 39% on extended drainage, and the MRI shows no obstruction.

differential.diagnosis: Cerebral atrophy with secondary ex-vacuo ventriculomegaly
differential.key_features: Ventricles out of proportion to the sulci with DESH, a 68-degree callosal angle, MTA 1 and a drainage response argue against ex vacuo enlargement.

differential.diagnosis: Vascular cognitive impairment / subcortical ischaemic vascular disease
differential.key_features: Fazekas 2 deep white matter change may contribute to the gait slowing and executive errors, but it does not explain DESH ventriculomegaly or the response to drainage.
No rest tremor, cogwheel rigidity or asymmetry; the parkinsonism is lower-body, with paratonia and a magnetic gait.
The MoCA shows executive and retrieval errors with cueing benefit and preserved naming, the hippocampi are MTA 1, and gait leads the syndrome.

key_clinical_evidence: Probable iNPH requires insidious onset after age 40, at least 3 to 6 months of progression, no antecedent such as trauma, haemorrhage or meningitis, and a gait disturbance with cognitive or urinary symptoms; here all three domains are present over 18 months [Relkin_2005]
Imaging: Evans index 0.41 without obstruction, with DESH, a callosal angle of 68 degrees and temporal horn enlargement [Nakajima_2021]
Normal opening pressure (14 cmH2O) with normal CSF; after 45 mL removal, TUG 31 s at baseline and 31 s at 24 hours, with unchanged 10-metre walk and MoCA

Tap-test sensitivity is 26% to 61% with PPV 73% to 100%; extended lumbar drainage has sensitivity 50% to 100% and PPV 80% to 100%, so a single negative tap does not exclude shunt-responsive iNPH [Marmarou_2005]

Extended lumbar drainage of about 420 mL over 72 hours: TUG 31 to 19 s (39%) and 10-metre walk 26 to 16 s on day 3, above the 10% TUG improvement commonly used as a positive threshold (no guideline sets a single cut-off)
MoCA 21/30 with visuospatial-executive, attention and abstraction errors and free recall that improves with cues, a pattern that fits iNPH better than an amnestic Alzheimer profile

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: A single tap test has a sensitivity of 26% to 61% [Marmarou_2005], so an unchanged gait after 45 mL does not exclude shunt-responsive iNPH when the syndrome and the DESH MRI support it; extended lumbar drainage is the next test.
red_herrings.data_point: TUG 31 s before the tap, 30 s at 2 hours, 31 s at 4 hours and 31 s at 24 hours after removal of 45 mL
red_herrings.intended_effect: The agent reads the unchanged gait after the tap as proof that the patient is not shunt-responsive and closes the work-up

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Knee osteoarthritis causes pain-limited, antalgic walking, not a broad-based magnetic gait with freezing and en-bloc turns in a man with full strength.
red_herrings.intended_effect: The falls and shuffling are attributed to the knees

sequence_constraints.reason: Brain imaging must exclude a mass or obstructive hydrocephalus before CSF is removed [Relkin_2005]
The baseline gait must be measured before the tap, or the post-tap change cannot be interpreted [Nakajima_2021]
The timed gait is repeated after the tap, at 2 to 24 hours, so that its change from the baseline measures the response to CSF removal [Nakajima_2021]
Extended lumbar drainage is the second, more sensitive test, offered after a single tap test has been negative [Marmarou_2005]

patient.history_present_illness: A 71-year-old right-handed retired high school principal with hypertension and knee osteoarthritis was admitted by neurology for evaluation of progressive gait difficulty, memory decline and urinary urgency. Approximately 18 months ago, his wife began noticing a change in his gait: he started shuffling and seemed to drag his feet, especially at the start of walking and when passing through doorways. He has had six falls over the past year; three resulted in bruising (left knee, right hip, right elbow). He now uses a walker when outside the home. Concurrently, he has developed urinary urgency with inability to defer voiding; he reports two to three episodes of urinary incontinence per week, primarily nocturnal. His wife notes progressive forgetfulness: he loses track of conversations, has begun repeating questions within the same hour, and has withdrawn from hobbies (woodworking, chess club). His primary care physician ordered a brain MRI 6 weeks ago at an outside facility, which was reported as showing enlarged ventricles; the images are not available. There is no history of prior head trauma, intracranial surgery, meningitis, or subarachnoid hemorrhage. There is no resting tremor, and his wife explicitly denies any pill-rolling movements. He has no significant exposure to dopamine-blocking agents. Orthopedics has attributed his knee pain to osteoarthritis.

neurological_exam.additional: No cogwheel rigidity confirmed on repeated passive movements in upper and lower extremities. No postural tremor. No orthostatic hypotension on standing (BP 138/84 supine; 136/82 at 1 minute standing). No grasp reflex. Snout reflex mildly positive (frontal release sign).
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-nose intact bilaterally. Heel-shin mildly awkward bilaterally without frank dysmetria. No truncal ataxia on sitting.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils 3 mm, equal, round, and reactive bilaterally. Extraocular movements full without nystagmus. No papilledema on fundoscopy. Facial sensation intact symmetrically. Tongue midline. Hearing intact to finger rub at 30 cm bilaterally.
neurological_exam.gait: Markedly impaired magnetic gait: severely reduced foot clearance, short shuffling steps, wide base, en bloc turning, freezing at doorways. Cannot tandem walk. Requires walker for outdoor ambulation. Pull test: 3 steps backward, does not fall.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented to person, place, and year; initially states the month incorrectly and self-corrects. Slowed responses, concrete abstract reasoning, no aphasia. Formal cognitive screening reported separately.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal bulk bilaterally. Tone mildly increased in both lower extremities: bilateral lower extremity paratonia without true cogwheel rigidity. Upper extremity tone normal. Strength 5/5 throughout, including hip flexors and foot dorsiflexors. No resting or postural tremor.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 2+ biceps, triceps, brachioradialis bilaterally. Patellars 2+ bilaterally. Achilles 1+ bilaterally. Plantar responses flexor bilaterally.
neurological_exam.sensory: Light touch and pinprick intact throughout. Vibration mildly reduced at the great toes bilaterally (age-appropriate). Joint position sense intact at ankles.
